verses.text: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond. It is engraved on the tablet of their heart, and on the horns of your altars.
Even their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles by the green trees on the high hills.
My mountain in the field, I will give your substance and all your treasures for a plunder, and your high places, because of sin, throughout all your borders.

You, even of yourself, shall discontinue from your heritage that I gave you. I will cause you to serve your enemies in the land which you don’t know, for you have kindled a fire in my anger which shall burn forever.”
Yahweh says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart departs from Yahweh.
For he shall be like a bush in the desert, and shall not see when good comes, but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land and not inhabited.
“Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh.

For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and shall not fear when heat comes, but its leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
The heart is deceitful above all things, and it is exceedingly corrupt. Who can know it?
“I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”
As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid, so is he who gets riches, and not by right; in the middle of his days they shall leave him, and at his end he shall be a fool.
A glorious throne, set on high from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
Yahweh, the hope of Israel, all who forsake you shall be disappointed. Those who depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken Yahweh, the spring of living waters.
Heal me, O Yahweh, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved: for you are my praise.
Behold, they tell me, “Where is Yahweh’s word? Let it be fulfilled now.”
As for me, I have not hurried from being a shepherd after you; neither have I desired the woeful day; you know. That which came out of my lips was before your face.
Don’t be a terror to me: you are my refuge in the day of evil.
Let them be disappointed who persecute me, but let not me be disappointed; let them be dismayed, but don’t let me be dismayed; bring on them the day of evil, and destroy them with double destruction.
Thus said Yahweh to me: “Go, and stand in the gate of the children of the people, through which the kings of Judah come in, and by which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem;
and tell them, ‘Hear Yahweh’s word, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates:
Yahweh says, “Be careful, and bear no burden on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
neither carry a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath day, neither do any work: but make the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
But they didn’t listen, neither turn their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, and might not receive instruction.
It shall happen, if you diligently listen to me,” says Yahweh, “to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but to make the Sabbath day holy, to do no work therein;

then shall there enter in by the gates of this city kings and princes sitting on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, they, and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city shall remain forever.

They shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places around Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the lowland, and from the hill country, and from the South, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meal offerings, and frankincense, and bringing sacrifices of thanksgiving, to Yahweh’s house.

But if you will not listen to me to make the Sabbath day holy, and not to bear a burden and enter in at the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.”’”

footnotes.content: Sin carved into stone—written so deep you can't rub it out with your thumb. Jeremiah names the hardness that comes when we turn away, when our own hearts become the tablets of our rebellion. Only Jesus, the living stone, could break through such hardness and write a new covenant there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The children grew up remembering the Asherah poles under the trees, not the Lord's law. Habit and inheritance run deep—we teach what we treasure, even when we don't mean to. Only grace can break the chain and plant new memory in a child's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land itself would be stripped because of sin—the fields, the treasures, all lost to plunder. God's judgment doesn't hover in the sky; it touches ground, home, the place where people root their lives. But He judges not to destroy forever, only to call back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They would be sent into exile, serving enemies in a land they didn't know—severed from their own soil, their own God. The fire of judgment kindled by their own hands would burn long. Yet even this exile, painful as it was, was God's strange mercy—not annihilation, but a furnace to purify.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursed is the one who trusts in flesh—a hard word, plainly spoken. We are so quick to lean on what we can see and touch, to make an arm of meat and bone our refuge. Jesus came in flesh, yet not to be our refuge; rather, to lead us to the Father who alone can hold us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A shrub in the desert, parched and small, missing every rain that could have saved it. This is the life of the one who turns from God—not destroyed all at once, but withering, isolated, unable to flourish no matter the season.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blessed—a word worth savoring—is the one whose confidence rests in Yahweh. Not in strength, wealth, reputation, or family name, but in Him. This blessedness isn't always loud or immediately seen, but it roots deep and holds when everything else gives way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A tree by the water—roots deep, leaf always green, unafraid of heat or drought. To trust God is to be planted in His presence, drawing living water that never fails. The heat comes anyway, but it cannot wither what is rooted in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heart is deceitful—we lie to ourselves more cleverly than anyone else ever could. We don't know our own motives, our own bent toward evil. But Jesus knew every heart He met, and still loved them. His knowledge of our hearts was always held within His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh searches the mind, tries the heart, sees the true fruit of our doings. This is both the most sobering and most comforting word—nothing is hidden from Him, yet He searches not as a judge hunting shame, but as a Father seeking to know His children truly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The partridge broods over eggs she didn't lay—a picture of empty stewardship, labor without real fruit. Those who gain wealth by wrong will watch it scatter like disturbed eggs. In the end, they'll be called fools, not for lacking riches, but for having loved them more than what's true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A glorious throne, set on high from the beginning—God's sanctuary is no afterthought, no contingency plan. It stood before the world's foundation, the place where His holiness dwells and mercy meets the broken. To know this throne exists is to know there is refuge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who forsake the spring of living waters will be written in the earth—names scrawled in dust that blows away. The tragedy isn't anger but absence, not punishment but the slow disappearance of those who turn from the only source of life. Jesus is that spring, offered freely to all who thirst.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah cries out: heal me, save me—raw, honest prayer from a man caught between God's word and a people unwilling to hear. His praise is not celebration but trust offered in the dark, knowing that the Lord's name alone is worth singing over, even in suffering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mockers demand: where is Yahweh's word? Let it come true now. They challenge God as though He owes them proof on their schedule. Jeremiah feels the sting of these taunts, bearing the weight of a word that comes to him faithfully but is scorned by those who hear it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have not hurried from being a shepherd after you—Jeremiah insists he has not sought the woeful day but stayed faithful to his calling, his words spoken before God's face. He defends not his comfort but his integrity, his faithfulness to the very word that brings him grief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't be a terror to me—Jeremiah's cry from exhaustion, not from doubt. He asks not for the trial to cease but for the Lord to remain his refuge within it. This is what keeps him going: not the absence of evil, but the presence of One greater than any terror.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A hard prayer for the enemies' shame and destruction—Jeremiah's anguish laid bare. Yet even this imprecation is brought to the Lord, not kept silent. He does not curse in his own strength but places the matter before Yahweh, trusting Him to judge what is just.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stand in the gate where kings enter and exit—the seat of power, the place where decisions are made. This is where Jeremiah must speak, not in a temple corner but in the center of the city's commerce and rule. The word of God belongs not hidden but proclaimed where it matters most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tell them to hear—the urgency of a word sent to the powerful. Kings, nobles, all Jerusalem: no one excuses themselves from what Yahweh will say. The gate becomes a pulpit, and refusal to listen is refusal to recognize who truly rules.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be careful, bear no burden on the Sabbath—a simple command that means something profound. The Sabbath is a test of obedience, yes, but also a weekly rehearsal of letting go, of trusting God's provision rather than our own anxious labor. To keep it holy is to say: I will rest in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No work on the Sabbath day—not merely rules for rules' sake, but a training in faith. One day a week, set apart, is to remind them that God sustains, not their hustle and strain. To keep the Sabbath holy is to believe that the world doesn't fall apart when we stop working.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They didn't listen, made their necks stiff—the same stubbornness described again and again. Not one failure but a pattern of willful turning away. The saddest words are these: they made themselves unable to hear, unwilling to learn, even when the Lord called.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you diligently listen, if you make the Sabbath holy—the great if. God always leaves room for turning around, for obedience, for choosing the way of life. Even in judgment, His call hangs open: listen to me, and it will be well.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Then shall enter kings and princes, riding in chariots, the city remaining forever—the promise of restoration for those who turn. Not a small thing: the throne of David would endure, Jerusalem would stand, but only for those who choose to hear and obey. Blessing is conditional on faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They would bring offerings from all around—burnt offerings, meal offerings, frankincense, sacrifices of thanksgiving. The whole nation, reunited, bringing their gifts to the house of Yahweh. This is the vision of what obedience could look like: a people drawn back to worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But if you will not listen—the final word, hard as stone. Fire will be kindled, palaces devoured, the gates become a place of burning. Readers today hear an echo in any place where mercy is offered and refused: God's patience is real, but His judgment is also real. The choice is ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
